findings.summary: Two changed files are outside the expected deliverables list: crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs and crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs.
findings.evidence: The list names crates/athena-core/src/brief.rs, which does not exist (`ls` fails). ReplayView and the verifier brief live in athena-context/src/briefs.rs, so changing that file is needed for criterion 4, and the plan listed it. The verify.rs edit only rewrites the held-finding text. Both are small and on-topic, but the deliverables list does not include them.

findings.summary: The parser does not accept a bare 'expected N%', which differs from the accepted reading's assumption and from the request's own example.
findings.evidence: The reading assumed that 'expected N%' or 'N% of newly refused' would both parse. The code requires 'N% [of] [the] newly refused'; a test asserts that "a candidate declaring 'expected 30%' is held" declares nothing. The stricter form fails safe (the 10% limit applies) and avoids reading quoted examples, such as this job's own criterion 1, as declarations. CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE and the CHANGELOG document the form. Still, a reader who writes only 'expected 80%' will be held without being told why.

findings.summary: The reason detector is a loose keyword match. In a refusal-rule job, almost any criterion with 'because' and 'refused' unlocks a share above 25%.
findings.evidence: The anchors include 'refuse', 'refused' and 'refusal', which refusal-rule criteria nearly always contain. For example, 'a reading without X is refused because the verifier cannot check it' would count as the reason. Showing the sentence to the verifier mitigates this, as the request intends. A stricter alternative is to require the reason in a dedicated form, such as a sentence that names past readings ('past readings ... because'), rather than treating generic refusal words as anchors.

findings.summary: The held-finding text in verify.rs still opens with 'more than 10%', which is wrong when the declared share is below 5%. The sentence is also hard to parse.
findings.evidence: The text reads 'more than {REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT}% of the newest N accepted readings are refused ..., more than the share the criteria declare (plus 5 points) or, when they declare none ..., more than that limit'. With declared 0% and 8% measured, the job is held but the message claims more than 10%.

findings.summary: CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE still tells readers to write the 'higher refusal rate is intended' sentence, which no longer has any effect on the gate.
findings.evidence: The old instruction is kept, followed by the new 'Say how many' instruction. It is harmless, but readers may think the phrase still matters.

summary: The change removes the phrase exemption (INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES and criteria_intend_higher_refusal no longer appear anywhere under crates/). A candidate can now declare 'expected N% of newly refused readings'. The replay holds it when the measured share exceeds the declared share by more than 5 points (exactly 5 over is not held), and holds it above 10% when no share is declared. A declared share above 25% applies only with a reason sentence, and the verifier brief shows the share and the reason above the replay list. I ran each planned targeted test (replay_declared, replay_phrase, replay_reason, replay_view_carries, replay_summary, changelog_describes_the_declared_share_rule) and all passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test (1587 tests) checks passed. All eight criteria are met. The findings are minor: briefs.rs and verify.rs are outside the deliverables list (which names a brief.rs that does not exist); the parser requires the 'of newly refused' form rather than a bare 'expected N%'; the reason detector is a loose keyword match; and the held-finding text in verify.rs still opens with 'more than 10%'. Verdict: pass.
